title: Wu et al. 2023: 2 m slabs bent by charges hung above them
summary: Eight 2 x 2 m, 100 mm reinforced concrete slabs spanning one way, the same steel in one layer near the underside or split between both faces, under 0.2 to 1.6 kg of TNT hung 0.25 to 0.5 m above (all at 0.43 m/kg^(1/3)). The underside's peak and residual displacement 300 mm from the centre. The charge loads the slab through the air: a coupled case.

sources.title: A research investigation into the impact of reinforcement distribution and blast distance on the blast resilience of reinforced concrete slabs
sources.used_for: The slabs, materials and charges (Tables 1-6, Figure 1) and the measured displacements (Table 10)

redistribution.note: Transcribed from an open-access paper (CC BY 4.0), with citation; nothing digitised from plots.

notes: The records swing upward 2-18 mm past where they started over some 60 ms, much more slowly than the slab's own period: something in the rig moved. Only the peak and the residual are given, and the residual carries that doubt.
The undersides of S6, S7 and D6 spalled over about 0.1 m^2, 4 cm deep.
The paper's contact shots (S1-S4, D1-D4), which holed every slab, are not included.
